title: On Bringing the news before supper
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：bring　|　正文 329 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bring 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the keeper ① bringed the news before supper before dawn, and every traveller in the tower said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the keeper ② brings the news before supper in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ bring the news before supper at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ bringed the news before supper before — a line in the calendar for January 1946 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Bringing the news before supper before dawn, the keeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ bring a storm about nothing in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Bring a storm about nothing at once and never mention it again.

By 1959 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the calendar, and a new traveller from the next tower ⑧ brings a storm about nothing before dawn every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the stair, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ bringed the news before supper again when nobody else would.

⑩ To bring the news before supper, my mother said in 1964, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the tower remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the tower forgets, somebody brings the news before supper in public again and somebody must bring the news before supper before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 带来（一般过去式 bringed the news before supper：1952 年守夜人头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 带来（一般现在 brings the news before supper：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 带来（不定式 to bring the news before supper：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 带来（过去完成时 had bringed the news before supper：1946 年一月的年历上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 带来（动名词 bringing the news before supper 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 招来（bring a storm about nothing：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去招来一场毫无来由的风波）
G. v. 招来（bring a storm about nothing：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 带来（后段两处：新来的过路人照例 brings a storm about nothing，而母亲又一次 bringed the news before supper）

answers.why: bring 意为“带来”，1952 年守夜人天没亮就带来晚饭前捎来的消息，那是钟楼里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 bringed。
bring 意为“带来”，自那以后守夜人当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 brings。
bring 意为“带来”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯带来晚饭前捎来的消息”，此处为不定式 to bring the news before supper。
bring 意为“带来”，年历里 一月 那行字说明早在 1959 年之前就有人带来过，故用过去完成时 had bringed。
bring 意为“带来”，守夜人说“带来晚饭前捎来的消息这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 bringing the news before supper 作主语。
bring 意为“招来”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去招来一场毫无来由的风波”，should ever 之后用原形 bring a storm about nothing。
bring 意为“招来”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻招来一场毫无来由的风波（bring a storm about nothing at once），以后再也不要提起。
bring 意为“带来”，新来的过路人每个年头都照例招来一场毫无来由的风波，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 brings。
bring 意为“带来”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就带来晚饭前捎来的消息，用一般过去式 bringed 叙述。
bring 意为“带来”，结尾那句是母亲 1964 年的话：要带来晚饭前捎来的消息，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和钟楼记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1952 年，守夜人天没亮就带来晚饭前捎来的消息；钟楼里每一个过路人都说这是头一回。（bringed the news before supper）
多年以后，守夜人仍当着众人面做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（brings the news before supper）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯带来晚饭前捎来的消息这件事本身。（to bring the news before supper）
早在 1946 年就有人带来晚饭前捎来的消息，一月那天年历上的一行字就是证据。（had bringed the news before supper）
守夜人说过，天没亮就带来晚饭前捎来的消息这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（bringing the news before supper 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻招来一场毫无来由的风波，以后再也不要提起。（bring a storm about nothing，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 bring 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1952 the keeper bringed the news before supper before dawn, and nobody in the tower forgot it.
Even now the keeper brings the news before supper in public whenever the tower asks.
Bringing the news before supper before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever bring a storm about nothing in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next tower brings a storm about nothing before dawn every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother bringed the news before supper again, and the tower remembered that half.
